newsitem.title: GERMANY: Viag sees small 1996 operating profits gain.
newsitem.headline: Viag sees small 1996 operating profits gain.

text.p: German industrial giant Viag AG confirmed on Thursday that operating profit for all of 1996 would improve somewhat over the 1995 figure.
Speaking to journalists at a dinner in Frankfurt, Viag's management board chairman Georg Obermeier said: "We expect the operating profit to be a little better than in 1995."

Viag said when it released its interim results in August that operating profits grew 10 percent in the first half of 1996, although a raft of one-off charges brought pre-tax profit down 21 percent to 1.178 billion marks for the period.
Obermeier was confident its consortium would win the fourth German mobile telephone licence, due to be awarded next year, as no other candidates had yet applied for the licence.
The consortium consists of RWE AG and British Telecom.

"If we don't get the licence, then we have a problem and the strategy we've been following up until now will be redundant. I am optimistic that we have a good chance of winning the licence," said Obermeier.

Asked if he expected dividends to increase from the 1995 level of 12 marks per share, Obermeier said: "Viag could possibly raise its dividend in 1996. The means are there. We'll have to see how the land lies when the time comes.
"There is more to shareholder value than just dividends -- share price performance is also important."
